The file on disk was replaced **4 s after the runner booted** with an older daemon that skips discovery whenever models are pinned. `runner/version.json` has said `0.1.0` since 2026‑10‑31, so no runner can tell that it runs stale code, and the self-updater never sees a newer version. The snapshot never deletes entries, so the dummy row stays forever. |
23|| 4 | Old `Unavailable` badge rather than "N runners" | `ModelSelector.jsx` lets `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` (the "Unavailable" verdict) win over `fleetCountBadgeNode`. The **harness** row ("Muse Code UNAVAILABLE") comes from the *backend container's* local CLI probe (`harnessAvailabilityBadgeNode` → backend `harnessDiscovery`), not from the fleet. The user wants pins to be **unverified / 0 runners** (survey q3/q4/q12). |

116|## 4. Work packages
117|
118|Each package lists: **Owns** (files, so parallel packages do not collide), **Change**, **Confirm bug (before)** (a failing test or check the implementer writes first), **Done when** (acceptance).
119|
120|### WP-A — Runner build identity and stale-code detection *(parallel)*
121|
122|**Why:** N1. Today a runner cannot say what code it runs, so merged fixes are invisible and the updater never fires.
123|
124|**Owns:** `runner/version.json`, the release/publish script that writes it (`scripts/` publish path used by `runner/updates`), `runner/daemon.js` → `factsFor().versions` **only**, `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js` (versions passthrough), the runner card in Settings (`frontend/src/components/settings/…Runner…`).
125|
126|**Change:**
127|1. Add `build` to the runner version: `{ runnerVersion, build: { sha, builtAt, dirty } }`. Stamp it at publish/bundle time. A dev runner started from a git checkout computes `sha` at boot (`git rev-parse HEAD`, plus `dirty` from `git status --porcelain runner/`).
128|2. Heartbeat `facts.versions` adds `build` and `bootedAtMs`. The runner also hashes its own `runner/` tree at boot. On each heartbeat it re-hashes cheaply (mtime scan) and reports `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` when files under its code dir changed after boot (the exact N1 failure).
129|3. The publish pipeline bumps `runnerVersion` on every release that touches `runner/**` or `api/agent/harnesses/**` (a CI check that fails the release if not), so `runner/updates` can actually offer updates.
130|4. Settings runner card shows build sha, and shows a warning when `build.sha` ≠ backend build sha or when `codeChangedSinceBoot` is true ("runner code changed on disk after start — restart / reinstall").
131|
132|**Confirm bug (before):** a unit test asserting `factsFor()` reports a build identity → fails today. Manual: §3.3.
133|
134|**Done when:** tests cover a sha in facts, `codeChangedSinceBoot` flipping after a file touch (temp dir fixture), normalizeCapabilities preserving `versions.build`, and the Settings warning rendering. Release CI rejects an unbumped version when runner code changed.
135|

138|### WP-B — Runner discovery reliability *(parallel)*
139|
140|**Why:** N2, N3, survey q5/q7. Discovery must always run, must not silently produce nothing, and must not depend on files the runner install lacks.
141|
142|**Owns:** `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`, `runner/daemon.js` → `refreshDiscoveredModels` + boot sequence **only**, `runner/config.js` (pin validation), runner bundle manifest / packaging (the list of files and deps shipped to runners), `runner/*.test.js` for these.
143|
144|**Change:**
145|1. **Boot self-check:** at startup, eagerly `import()` every discovery-leg module for the configured harnesses. A missing module or package becomes an explicit `discoveryStatus[h] = { ok:false, error:{ code:'LEG_MODULE_MISSING', … } }` right away, rather than surfacing on the first lazy import 12 h later. Log it loudly.
146|2. **Never-ran is visible:** `getDiscoveryStatus(harnessIds)` returns an entry for **every configured harness**. A harness that has not completed a round reports `{ ok:false, error:{ code:'NOT_YET_RUN' } }`, never `{}`. An outer `catch` in `refreshDiscoveredModels` records `ROUND_FAILED` on every configured harness instead of only logging.
147|3. **Packaging:** ship the leg dependencies with the runner bundle. Either vendor the leg's model-listing code into `runner/`, or include `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (and the agy/vibe/opencode catalog modules) in the bundle's dependency manifest. Add a bundle test that imports every leg from the packaged tree.
148|4. **Staleness marker (q5):** each slice carries `atMs`. When `now − atMs > KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISCOVERY_STALE_MS` (default 24 h), the slice keeps its ids but reports `stale:true` in `discoveryStatus`. WP-C then stops counting those ids as verified. **No eviction on the runner.** The catalogue keeps history (q1).
149|5. **Canonical pins (q7/q8):** `runner/config.js` validates `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` / `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`. Any id that does not parse as `harness` / `harnessReasoning` form, or whose harness is not in `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESSES`, is **dropped with a boot warning** and listed in `facts.errors`. This means `deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud` and `ollama-cloud-direct::gemma4:31b-cloud` can no longer be advertised.
150|6. Confirm (test) that a pinned runner still scans (`resolveAdvertisedModels` = pin ∪ discovered), and that `requestModelRediscovery` triggers a fresh round (q11).
151|
152|**Confirm bug (before):**
153|- Test: config with `models:['muse::meta::a']`, discovery leg fake that throws on import → `getDiscoveryStatus(['muse'])` returns `{}` today (should name the error).
154|- Test: `loadConfig` with `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS=deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud` → accepted today (should be rejected with a warning).
155|
156|**Done when:** those tests pass; a bundle-import test passes against the packaged runner tree; `discoveryStatus` always has one key per configured harness.

160|### WP-C — Backend catalogue contract: canonical ids, per-harness attribution, verified counts, lifecycle *(parallel; single owner of these files)*
161|
162|**Why:** N4, N5 (lifecycle half), N6 (contract half), survey q1/q3/q4/q6/q7/q8/q12/q13.
163|
164|**Owns:** `api/flow/dispatch/catalogIngest.js`, `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js`, `api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.js` (catalogue-facing verdicts only), `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js` (catalogue routes only), and their tests. **Dispatch (`buildFleetModelCatalog`, `runnerMatches/*`) is not touched in this package** (see WP-G).
165|
166|**Change:**
167|1. **Canonical ids only (q7/q8):** `ingestAdvertisedId` accepts only `harness` / `harnessReasoning` forms. `bare` / `provider` forms are quarantined with reason `"not harness-qualified (want harness::provider::model[::effort])"`. Ids whose harness is not in the runner's reported harness list are quarantined with reason `"harness not served by runner <id>"`.
168|2. **Per-entry attribution:** `entry.harnesses = [parsed.harness]`. Stop copying the runner's harness list (`catalogIngest.js:101`, `fleetModelSnapshot.js:213-224`). Tiers stay per runner.
169|3. **Verified counts (q3/q4/q12):** an entry's `runnerCount` / `runnerIds` include only claim-eligible runners whose own discovery **confirmed** the id (`modelProvenance` has it, and the leg is not `stale` per WP-B). Pinned/allowlisted-but-unconfirmed claimants go to a new `declaredBy: [runnerIds]`, with `verified: runnerCount > 0`. The existing `claimedBy` (stale pins) stays.

Read text file `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`.
1|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — Runner catalogue creation bug
2|
3|Task: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`  
4|Stage: investigation + replication & structural fix proposal (docs-only)  
5|Inputs: bug report (`assets/image.png`), `SURVEY.md`, task spec, plus repo history and prior tickets (notably `9d2b75a2-1ecd-47ce-a9f9-b3068c5f5cf7`).
6|
7|## Scope
8|
9|This report is investigatory. It proposes possible *causes* of the runner catalogue defect, assesses replicability/testability, and proposes the shape of a structural long-term fix. No code is changed in this stage.
10|
11|The reported symptoms are:
12|
13|- newly released harness models (e.g. `muse-ember`) never appear;
14|- dummy/test models appear in production catalogue views;
15|- broken harness models from other harnesses appear in places they should not (e.g. `gemma4`, `deepseek`);
16|- models that are available are still shown with the old “unavailable” flag instead of “how many runners serve it”;
17|- repeated backend/runner restarts and prior tickets did not durably correct it.
18|
19|The intended flow is:
20|
21|```
22|runner harness scan → discoveredModelsCache → heartbeat facts.models
23|  → runnerRegistry capabilities → fleet snapshot (/runners/models/catalogue)
24|  → frontend withFleetModels / fleetCountBadgeNode
25|```
26|
27|## Evidence base
28|
29|- `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` (discovery legs, cache slicing, validation)
30|- `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels`, `resolveAdvertisedModels`)
31|- `runner/daemon.js` (`refreshDiscoveredModels`, `factsFor`, keep-old behaviour)
32|- `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` (`heartbeat`, persisted `_persist`, capabilities)
33|- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
34|- `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` / `fleetModelCatalog.js`
35|- `api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.js`
36|- `frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/*`, `frontend/src/services/modelStatus.js`
37|- Prior ticket root cause: `docs/tasks/9d2b75a2-1ecd-47ce-a9f9-b3068c5f5cf7/ROOT_CAUSE.md`
38|
39|---
40|
41|## Candidate cause 1 — “keep previous slice” cache semantics create sticky stale/dummy ids and hide brand-new models
42|
43|### Summary
44|
45|Discovery on each leg is deliberately non-destructive: `runDiscoveryLeg` keeps the *previous* per-harness slice on failure, empty result, unparseable output, or grammar-invalid incoming ids. `refreshDiscoveredModels` then keeps the global `discoveredModelsCache` when the combined round is empty. Persisted backend `fleetModelSnapshot.js` additionally keeps stale entries as *unavailable* rather than deleting them.
46|
47|### Why this could be the bug
48|
49|- Pros:
50|  - A transient scan failure can never erase a known-good menu, so operators reasonably see old models “forever” after a bad scan.
51|  - A scan that once returned a dummy id (mock/test model, stale manual pin) is retained unless a later round replaces it; the UI therefore still shows it in catalogue views.
52|  - New models (e.g. `muse-ember`) only appear when the *next successful* round both succeeds and validates them; empty/failed rounds leave the previous cache, so release cadence alone cannot clear the gap.
53|  - Backend side: `fleetModelSnapshot.update` only flips previously available-but-now-unserved entries to unavailable; it never deletes them, so old ids remain in `/runners/models/catalogue` as `Unavailable` instead of being replaced by live `runnerCount` entries. This matches the observed “old unavailable flag”.
54|- Cons / counter-evidence:
55|  - The design intentionally keeps history (survey round 1 answer notes users *want* dropped models to remain visible with `0 runners`), so “keep but mark unavailable” is partly desired behaviour, not purely a defect.
56|  - The cache is replaceable when a round succeeds (`combinedIds.length > 0`), so a healthy runner *should* eventually refresh it; sticky staleness requires a continuous scan failure or cache desync.
57|- References:
58|  - `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` — `runDiscoveryLeg` (keep previous on empty/invalid/failure), `runDiscoveryRound`
59|  - `runner/daemon.js` — `refreshDiscoveredModels` (`if (combinedIds.length > 0) { discoveredModelsCache = combinedIds; }`)
60|  - `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` — `update()` marks non-live entries `available: false` instead of deleting
61|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (d) pin-wins + TTL cadence; suspect corridor “empty round keeps cache”
62|
63|### Replicability
64|
65|Replicable without prod. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §1 and `TESTING_GUIDE.md` §1. Unit-testable by seeding `discoveryCache` with a dummy id, simulating a failed/empty leg, and asserting the dummy survives.
66|
67|---
68|
69|## Candidate cause 2 — Operator allowlist (`availableModels`) replaces the advertised list and is trusted as servable
70|
71|### Summary
72|
73|`effectiveRunnerModels` uses `operatorConfig.availableModels` instead of `runner-reported` models whenever set. `confirmRunnerModel` always marks operator-asserted ids as `unknown` (trusted) so they become available even when no discovery slice listed them. The backend persisted runner records (and local state file) also retain the allowlist independently of heartbeats.
74|
75|### Why this could be the bug
76|
77|- Pros:
78|  - A stale or hand-entered allowlist can expose ids that no harness currently serves (including dummy/test, `gemma4`, `deepseek`) because `effectiveRunnerModels` no longer consults the scanned menu.
79|  - Operator assertions are never contradicted by the runner’s own discovery, so they ride through fleet snapshot ingestion and appear in the catalogue as valid entries with non-zero runner counts.
80|  - Conversely, a stale allowlist can hide newly discovered models when it does not include them (or when discovery is disabled with `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs: 0`), so new releases are omitted.
81|  - Persisted `runners.json` / `lastSeenAt = null` after backend restart means old capability lists or allowlists can survive in a degraded form, and the fleet snapshot can continue carrying entries until heartbeats overwrite it.
82|- Cons / counter-evidence:
83|  - This behaviour is by design: it exists to let operators serve models an under-reporting runner cannot discover.
84|  - The allowlist is operator-provided, not runner-generated; if the reported dummy models are truly “test models”, some other mechanism must seed them.
85|- References:
86|  - `api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches/effectiveRunnerModels.js`
87|  - `api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.js` — operator-asserted ids trust rule
88|  - `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` — `normalizeOperatorConfig`, `availableModels`, persisted state (`_loadState`/`_persist`)
89|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (g) operator allowlist shadow
90|
91|### Replicability
92|
93|Replicable without prod. Set `availableModels: ["deepseek::deepseek::fake", "muse::meta::dummy"]` on a runner, heartbeat, and observe catalogue. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §2.
94|
95|---
96|
97|## Candidate cause 3 — Grammar/filtering mismatches across legs drop valid new models and leak invalid ones
98|
99|### Summary
100|
101|Different parts of the chain apply different validity rules to model ids:
102|
103|- runner muse leg (`runner/modelDiscovery.js`) previously rejected any provider/model containing `:` — now fixed to reject only `::` but other legs still differ in edge cases;
104|- backend MSP parser (`api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/...`) does not filter `:` ;
105|- shared grammar allows single `:` in ids;
106|- several backend transforms (`shared/modelKeys.js:withModelKey`) throw on `::`, which can discard a whole agy/vibe result set;
107|- frontend `fleetModelsForHarness` creates synthesized entries from snapshot ids without re-validating against the backend harness section.
108|
109|### Why this could be the bug
110|
111|- Pros:
112|  - A newly released model whose provider/model id contains `:` (common for cloud-tagged models) can be dropped by one leg while other paths retain it, so the runner never pushes it to the catalogue. The reverse mismatch can make a model present in one view but absent elsewhere.
113|  - The muse-vs-rest asymmetry explains why “muse-ember” and models like `gemma4`/`deepseek` drift between harness sections.
114|  - The strict section gate in `fleetModelsForHarness` drops ids when serving harnesses do not include the rendered harness, so a runner that advertises an id for the wrong harness causes silent disappearance.
115|  - Dummy/test models can remain if they are grammatically valid but no longer real (keep-old behaviour compounds this), with no authority to reconcile against live harness menus.
116|- Cons / counter-evidence:
117|  - The filter bug alone does not explain stale *persistence* after the list should update, or the disappearance of the `runnerCount` display focus.
118|  - Backend MSP has no colon filter and therefore already handles `:` correctly, so a pure colon filter only explains runner leg omission, not leakages from backend models.
119|- References:
120|  - `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels` colon filter — now `::`-only)
121|  - `shared/modelKeys.js` (parse rules, `withModelKey`, throws on `::`)
122|  - `frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/fleetModelsForHarness.js` (serving harness gate)
123|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (c), section 3 “other-leg audit”
124|
125|### Replicability
126|
127|Replicable without prod. Inject a `muse serve` row with `modelId: "muse-ember:cloud"` and verify leg output. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §3.
128|
129|---
130|
131|## Candidate cause 4 — Catalogue representation still mixes two presentation contracts (old `unavailable` vs runner-count)
132|
133|### Summary
134|
135|The UI now treats fleet availability as runner count (`fleetCountBadgeNode`) while persisted snapshot entries retain and expose an explicit `available: false` + `unavailableReason`. Components consult `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` first, so older/cached snapshot rows can badge “Unavailable” even when the count/runner data has changed.
136|
137|### Why this could be the bug
138|
139|- Pros:
140|  - Inconsistent rendering means a model can still display the old unavailable badge in a picker even though its snapshot/counts should now say `N runners`.
141|  - Because the snapshot marks non-live entries unavailable and never removes them, the “old unavailable flag” directly persists as `available: false`, while the count (`runnerCount`) is reset to 0, making a valid current model look unavailable if snapshot refresh is delayed or uses stale runner input.
142|  - This is consistent with the user’s stated requirement: replace “unavailable” with “how many runners have that harness/model available”.
143|- Cons / counter-evidence:
144|  - This is primarily a frontend presentation/reporting issue. It explains display, not necessarily why new models are missing from the underlying catalogue.
145|  - The count badge still renders `0 runners`, so counts are technically shown even when unavailable.
146|- References:
147|  - `frontend/src/services/modelStatus.js` (`fleetSnapshotBadge`, `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode`, `fleetCountBadgeNode`)
148|  - `frontend/src/hooks/useFleetModelCatalog/fleetCountsById.js`
149|  - `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` (`available`, `unavailableReason`, `runnerCount`)
150|  - `SURVEY.md` q3 notes
151|
152|### Replicability
153|
154|Replicable without prod (frontend unit test) and with a snapshot reload (backend restart without heartbeats). See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §4.
155|
156|---
157|
158|## Cross-cutting observations
159|
160|- Multiple historical tickets (see `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md`) repeatedly fixed piecewise symptoms (colon filter, stale pins, unavailable badges) but preserved the architectural invariants above. Any one of them failing can reproduce the entire visible defect, which explains why small fixes did not durably resolve it.
161|- The backend and runner use different cadences/caches; structural reconciliation would need a clear invalidation/replacement contract across discovery slices, runner facts, registry capabilities, and persisted fleet snapshots.
162|
163|## Bottom line
164|
165|At least four interacting mechanisms are plausible root causes, and the defect likely involves more than one:
166|
167|1. keep-old cache behaviour retaining stale/dummy models;
168|2. operator allowlists bypassing and contradicting discovery;
169|3. grammar/filter mismatches between discovery, heartbeat, and fleet ingestion;
170|4. mixed `available` vs runner-count presentation with persisted snapshot staleness.
171|
172|These should be examined together in the structural fix.
173|
174|---
175|
176|## Structural long-term fix — proposal (docs-only, not yet implemented)
177|
178|The recurring failure mode is: **no single source of truth and no clear lifecycle** for "which models are real right now". Each layer (leg slice → global cache → heartbeat → registry → fleet snapshot → frontend section) has its own keep-old, trust-allowlists, or mark-unavailable-not-delete rule. Piecewise patches to one layer cannot fix the others. A durable fix needs a structural contract.
179|
180|### Principles
181|
182|1. **One canonical lifecycle:** `discovered → advertised → registered → catalogued → displayed` with explicit TTL/eviction at each step, not implicit keep-old.
183|2. **Provenance everywhere:** every model id carries *who saw it, when, via which leg/harness*, so stale/dummy entries are attributable.
184|3. **No silent keep-old without expiry:** a cached entry that is not reconfirmed within a bounded window is either evicted or demoted to `available: false` with a countdown to deletion, not retained forever.
185|4. **Grammar validated once, at the edge:** normalize/validate at discovery ingestion; downstream layers never re-filter or re-invent validity.
186|5. **Counts, not flags, as primary UX:** frontend renders `runnerCount` as truth; `available/unavailable` is derived, never stored as independent flag.
187|
188|### Recommended shape (4 layers)
189|
190|#### Layer A — Runner discovery: slice TTL + explicit eviction
191|
192|- Each `discoveryCache[harnessId]` entry gets `atMs` + `ttlMs` (e.g. 24 h, configurable via `KAINBAIN_DISCOVERY_TTL_MS`).
193|- `runDiscoveryLeg` on **successful non-empty** round: replaces slice (current behaviour).
194|- `runDiscoveryLeg` on **failure/empty/invalid**: keeps previous slice *but* records `error` and checks TTL. If `now - atMs > ttlMs`, the slice is **evicted** (set to `[]` with `error: STALE_EVICTED`), not kept indefinitely.
195|- `refreshDiscoveredModels` combined cache: same TTL gate. Optionally add a `forceRefresh` heartbeat field so the backend can request re-probe.
196|- Telemetry: expose `getDiscoveryStatus()` with `ageMs`, `ttlMs`, `error` per harness so Settings can show "stale (12 h old, next eviction in 12 h)".
197|
198|#### Layer B — Heartbeat advertisement: pin semantics made explicit
199|
200|- Keep `resolveAdvertisedModels` pin-UNION-discovered default, but:
201|  - Tag each advertised id with source: `pin` vs `discovered` vs `allowlist` (via a parallel `advertisedProvenance` map, not just a string label).
202|  - When `operatorConfig.availableModels` is set, the backend should still **record** the discovery list alongside the allowlist (new field `discoveredModels` in capabilities) so divergence is observable.
203|  - Add an operator warning when allowlist and discovery disagree (e.g. allowlist id not seen in discovery for > TTL).
204|
205|#### Layer C — Backend fleet snapshot: single ingestion point with quarantine and retention policy
206|
207|- Already partially exists (`fleetModelSnapshot.js` quarantine + `FLEET_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MODELS` eviction). Extend:
208|  - **Grammar gate once:** `catalogIngest.js` validates every incoming `facts.models` against `shared/modelKeys.js` grammar. Malformed ids go to `quarantined` with reason, never to `models`.
209|  - **Stale-pin detection:** `runnerModelConfirmation` already exists — keep it, but surface `staleAdvertReason` in snapshot `unavailableReason` so UI can say "advertised by runner X but never discovered by it".
210|  - **Retention policy:** replace "mark unavailable forever" with: mark `available: false` immediately, but evict entries that stay unavailable for `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_RETENTION_MS` (e.g. 14 days, to satisfy the "keep dropped models at 0 runners for deprecation" requirement) — configurable, with oldest-unavailable-first eviction when cap exceeded.
211|  - **Restart behaviour:** after backend restart, snapshot reloads as unavailable until heartbeats reconfirm (current), but with visible `lastSeenAtMs` age so UI can show "waiting for runners to re-report (X min ago)".
212|
213|#### Layer D — Frontend: count-first rendering, no dual truth
214|
215|- Frontend `fleetCountsById` + `fleetCountBadgeNode` is already the intended new contract ("how many runners have that harness/model"). Complete the migration:
216|  - Remove any `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` "Unavailable" badge from picker rows; replace with `N runners` / `0 runners — not currently served` (grey, but not an error badge).
217|  - Quarantined ids never render as selectable options (only in diagnostics/Settings if exposed).
218|  - Stale-pin / retention-warning ids render with a subtle annotation ("advertised but not discovered by runner") not a blocking badge.
219|
220|### Migration checklist
221|
222|- [ ] Add `KAINBAIN_DISCOVERY_TTL_MS` + eviction in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` + `runner/daemon.js`.
223|- [ ] Add `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_RETENTION_MS` + eviction in `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js`.
224|- [ ] Make `catalogIngest` the single grammar gate; remove downstream re-filtering.
225|- [ ] Surface `discoveredModels` alongside `availableModels` in registry; warn on divergence.
226|- [ ] Frontend: retire `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` "Unavailable" as primary badge in pickers.
227|- [ ] Add persistence tests: backend restart → snapshot → heartbeat reconfirm → eviction.
228|
229|### Why this survives repeated tickets
230|
231|- TTL+eviction bounds staleness even if one leg stays broken.
232|- Single grammar gate prevents per-leg drift.
233|- Provenance makes "where did this dummy id come from?" answerable without guessing.
234|- Retention window satisfies the deprecation-visibility requirement (0 runners) without permanent clutter.
235|- Count-first UX removes the old "unavailable" flag as a source of confusion.
236|
237|---
238|
239|## Replicability & testability summary
240|
241|All four candidate causes are replicable **without touching prod or invoking real agents**. See the companion guides:
242|
243|- `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` — quick manual replication steps per symptom (all flagged where prod/real-agent invocation would be needed, and not attempted here).
244|- `TESTING_GUIDE.md` — runnable test examples (TDD-style) for each cause, including what needs a harness mock vs a real CLI spawn.
245|
246|If a symptom cannot be reproduced under mock conditions, the guide flags it and describes what a prod-safe reproduction would look like (with explicit permission required).
